reason: The CIF parses and primitive-standardizes as claimed (P1, 20 fully occupied sites, Sr4Ta4N4O8, V = 226.224 A^3), and its monoclinic cell gives strong peak-position coverage, but the submitted atomic realization is not viable or sufficiently established. Its periodic geometry contains pervasive demonstrably impossible contacts, including O-O = 1.198 A, N-N = 1.199 A, multiple other anion-anion contacts of 1.31-1.72 A, Sr-O = 1.545 A, Sr-N = 1.550-1.587 A, and Ta-anion distances near 1.59 A; the trace itself found these contacts in the final coordinate model yet still submitted it. The trace reports only custom stick/intensity objectives for the final model, not a comparable instantiated whole-profile refinement. A direct fixed-intensity profile comparison of the submitted CIF gives an optimized unweighted profile residual of about 20.5%, versus 5.6% with free intensities at the same indexed reflection positions (13.4 times the residual variance), with important intensity mismatches. Thus good indexing does not rescue the chemically invalid, poorly supported coordinates and O/N ordering, and another structure-solution attempt is likely to add a materially different viable candidate.
